newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SIMSMETAL SAYS AUSTRALIAN DLR FALL HELPFUL.
newsitem.headline: SIMSMETAL SAYS AUSTRALIAN DLR FALL HELPFUL.

text.p: Metals recycler Simsmetal Ltd said on Tuesday it expected the recent fall in the Australian dollar to help its results in the first half of 1997/98 (July/June).
"We've budgeted for US$0.77, so anything lower is good for us," Simsmetal chief executive John Crabb told a news briefing.
A one cent move in the Australian dollar translates into a A$2 million change in Simsmetal's profit before interest and tax.
Earlier Simsmetal released its unaudited 1996/97 results showing a 25 percent fall in net profit to A$35.17 million.
Profit before interest and tax fell 21 percent to A$57.64 million on 19 percent higher sales volume of 4.7 million tonnes.
Crabb said the company remained on the lookout for acquisitions, although it was wary of current prices being paid, particularly in the United States.

"You really have to be patient, you have to be prepared to say no and you have to be prepared to keep looking for the sweet ones that fall off the tree. They are there but you just have to keep looking for them," Crabb said.
The company's acquisitions in Britain include Dorset-based metals group D.G. Corbin and Sons.
In the United States, the company is set to complete the acquisition of Peck Recycling in Virginia during September 1997.
Crabb said that while Simsmetal would be able to digest an acquisition as large as A$150 million, the nature of the industry meant a buy of that size was unlikely.
"I don't think Simsmetal would be frightened, if the appropriate acquisition came along, if it cost A$140 million to A$150 million. It wouldn't knock us about that much," he said.
"You have to look at our business. While some of the businesses could be as high as A$100 million there have not been too many metal recycling companies sold at that level," he said.
Crabb said Simsmetal had unused credit lines and had never tapped shareholders apart from a dividend reinvestment plan, reintroduced with current results after being suspended for several years.
By 1.20 p.m. (0320 GMT), Simsmetal shares were five cents higher at A$10.35, having earlier touched a record high A$10.36.
